title: Transport and Channel Normal Forms for Clifford Interactions
authors: Xiong Chunhe, Kim Sunho, Zhang Qing-Hua, Fei Shao-Ming, Wu Junde
abstract: We study how Clifford interactions with a fixed environment determine quantum transmission, in a setting that extends positive discrete quantum convolution . We characterize when Clifford operations on the environment can be replaced by operations on the signal input and the two outputs, and classify the interactions under local Clifford transformations . For pure stabilizer environments, we determine the noiseless, dephasing, and completely depolarizing parts of the channel directly from the interaction and environmental stabilizers, obtaining its quantum and private capacities . This reveals a distinction between interactions: those locally equivalent to positive convolution produce entanglement-breaking channels for every pure stabilizer environment, whereas every other interaction in the class admits noiseless quantum transmission with a suitable pure stabilizer environment . For positive convolution, environmental Clifford transport also allows us to separate the stabilized coordinates of an arbitrary mixed environment . These coordinates carry only a classical label shared by the receiver and environment, so removing them preserves quantum and private capacities . The resulting channel reduction yields a private-capacity bound by the modified relative entropy of magic of the environmental state .
summary: This work characterizes quantum channels generated by Clifford interactions with an environment using tools from symplectic geometry. It develops a 'channel normal form' to classify these interactions based on their information-theoretic properties. The findings distinguish between different interaction types, providing new bounds on quantum and private capacities.
main_problem: The paper characterizes quantum information transmission through channels induced by bipartite Clifford interactions with an environment, extending concepts from positive discrete quantum convolution.
main_result: It establishes a classification of these interactions, showing a key distinction: those locally equivalent to positive convolution yield entanglement-breaking channels, while others support noiseless quantum transmission.
method: The analysis employs symplectic geometry, Weyl operators, and the development of a 'channel normal form' to analyze the channel action $ho  oxtimes_S \sigma$.
model_or_system: The system models quantum channels defined by Clifford interactions involving signal input ($A$), environment input ($B$), and corresponding outputs ($A', B'$), analyzed using symplectic matrices $S \in 	ext{Sp}(V \oplus V)$.
key_observables: Quantum and private capacities, the cross-ratio invariant, and the modified relative entropy of magic.
important_parameters: The regularity of the interaction matrix $S$, and the structure of the environmental stabilizers.
main_assumptions: The analysis focuses specifically on Clifford interactions and assumes the initial independence of the signal and environment.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the channel as a two-input/two-output system, and Figure 2 shows the Clifford transport identity, relating environmental change to signal-input and two output Cliffords.
paper_structure: The paper develops the framework using symplectic geometry, proves identities for convolution and transport, establishes a transport criterion based on the cross-ratio, and finally derives capacity bounds using the modified relative entropy of magic.
why_interesting: The rigorous mathematical framework connecting symplectic geometry to channel capacity provides powerful tools for understanding decoherence and information flow in open quantum systems, which is highly relevant to quantum optics and open quantum systems.
